blocks.text: HAGONOY, Bulacan — More than 300 residents marched through the streets of this municipality early Sunday to mark the first anniversary of Tindig Hagonoy, renewing their call for justice over alleged corruption in flood control projects and for concrete solutions to the town’s chronic flooding problem. The protesters also called for accountability over the alleged billion-peso “ghost” flood control projects they blamed for worsening flooding that has repeatedly submerged much of the town, leaving residents helpless. Seventy-two-year-old Amando Saguinsin, a lay minister at the National Shrine of St. Anne, joined other members of the group in calling for an end to […]...
